case_title: Chinnam Kameswara Rao and Ors. v. State of A.P. (rep. by Home Secretary)
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: an altercation the previous day (over palmyrah nuts), after which an accused threatened the deceased with dire consequences
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.324 r/w s.34 (charged as s.302 and s.324 per p.2; p.7 refers to s.302 and s.307)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured witness PW-1 and PWs 2, 3, 4, 6); post-mortem; seizure of weapons; circumstantial (prior threat, lying in wait)
aggravating_circumstances: Head injuries to a vital part causing skull fracture; assault continued after the deceased fell; premeditated attack
high_court_outcome: State's appeal partly allowed: acquittal of appellants reversed and convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 and s.324 r/w s.34 IPC; acquittal of A-4 affirmed
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.34); attempt/hurt under IPC s.324 r/w s.34
neutral_facts: On an evening in late April, four men stopped the victim and a second man while they were walking home at a park centre. The previous day, the same parties had quarrelled while the victim and the second man were collecting palmyrah nuts from fields. A shopkeeper in the vicinity intervened and pacified them, though one of the accused allegedly threatened the victim with dire consequences. On the following evening, the accused allegedly confronted the victim and the second man. Three of the accused were armed with stout casuarina sticks; the fourth was unarmed. An altercation followed, and one accused allegedly struck the victim on the head. When the second man intervened, two others allegedly struck him on the head with sticks. Both men fell. The fourth accused allegedly kicked and punched the victim, while the three armed men continued hitting both of them. The assailants then ran away towards the house of one of them, believing both men dead. Four persons were said to have witnessed the incident. The injured were taken to a government hospital, where the victim's statement was recorded. The victim died of his injuries in the early hours of the next day. The investigation included arrest of the accused, post-mortem examination of the body, and seizure of the weapons of offence.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from head injuries including skull fracture; the second man (PW-1) was also injured with bleeding head injuries
premeditation_planning: Yes: court found the attack premeditated and preconcerted, given the prior threat, lying in wait, and fetching hidden sticks
motive: The incident was a sequel to the previous day's confrontation and threat (accepted by the court)
key_evidence_accepted: Depositions of eyewitnesses PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4 and PW-6; PW-3 as witness to the prior threat; evidence of lying in wait; nature of head injuries
witness_credibility: PW-1 (injured) found credible; trial court erred in rejecting eyewitness testimony over minor contradictions that did not shatter credibility
post_offence_conduct: Fled the scene after believing both victims were dead
trial_duration: offence: 27 April 2003; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 8 February 2011; Supreme Court: 10 January 2013
legal_representation: Appellants: M.S. Ganesh (senior counsel) and T. Anamika. State: D. Mahesh Babu, Mayur Shah, Savita Devi, Suchitra Hrangkhawl, Amit K. Nain, M.B. Shivdu
investigation_status: Case registered on victim's hospital statement; investigation completed (arrests, post-mortem, weapon seizure); charge sheet filed; trial completed with 13 prosecution witnesses and no defence evidence
procedural_irregularity: Section 34 was not in the charge against the appellants; court held no prejudice was shown, so the conviction's legality was unaffected
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted all accused. High Court: appellants' acquittal reversed and convicted (s.302/34 and s.324/34 IPC); A-4 acquittal affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, convictions upheld
defence_argument: High Court wrongly re-appraised evidence and reversed acquittal; conviction under s.302/307 r/w s.34 invalid as s.34 was not charged, causing prejudice; no evidence of common intention to murder, so at most s.304 culpable homicide
legal_principle_applied: Appellate court has full power under s.386 CrPC to re-appraise evidence; if the trial court's acquittal was not a reasonably possible view, it may reverse; absence of s.34 charge causes no prejudice unless shown; common intention may be premeditated
precedent_relied_upon: Dhanna v. State of MP (1996) 10 SCC 79; Kallu @ Masih v. State of MP (2006) 10 SCC 313; Murugesan v. State 2012 (10) SCALE 378; Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415; Krishna Govind Patil v. State of Maharashtra AIR 1963 SC 1413; Darbara Singh v. State of Punjab 2012 (8) SCALE 649; Gurpreet Singh v. State of Punjab (2005) 12 SCC 615
judicial_aggravating_factors: Premeditated, preconcerted attack; prior threat; lying in wait; vital-part head injuries; continued assault after the victim fell
